newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil forecasters still see no frosts for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil forecasters still see no frosts for coffee.

text.p: The outlook for an approaching polar air mass remains unchanged with no frosts forecast for Brazil's coffee areas, local meteorologists said.

Temperatures are expected to fall early Friday morning in the north of Parana but cloud cover will prevent any formation of frosts, said Marcos Massari, meteorologist at independent forecasters Somar.
Early Saturday morning, temperatures will also fall in Sao Paulo and south Minas Gerais but again no frost is forecast.
The arrival of another cold front in Parana increasing cloud cover also means that temperatures on May 24 in the north of the state will not fall to critical levels, he added.
By May 25, temperatures should begin to pick up again, Massari said.
Brazil's National Institute of Meteorology also said there was no frost forecast in Brazil's coffee regions in the coming days.
The center of the approaching air mass, currently over Argentina, has an intensity of 1,028 millibars.
A second air mass, currently of 1,030 millibars, is expected to enter Brazil's southern states of Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina on May 25.

But as it is coming in from the sea, it will carry a great deal of humidity and so is expected to weaken quickly, again posing no frost threat for the coffee regions, Massari said. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
